qualifying_updates.title: Automatic Dependabot access to GitHub-hosted registries
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub re-enabled automatic GitHub Packages authentication for Dependabot jobs. Dependabot can request packages:read through GITHUB_TOKEN for GitHub-hosted registries, reusing repository access granted through Manage Actions access, while fallback behavior avoids overriding explicit registry credentials.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding agents and dependency-update bots increasingly operate inside the same source workflow. This update reduces PAT handling for automated dependency work and gives source-workflow pages a concrete example of least-privilege package access, fallback authentication, and credential-removal hygiene.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Dependency automation guidance can recommend repository-scoped package grants over long-lived PAT registry entries when the package is hosted in GitHub Packages.
follow_up_notes: Check whether source-workflows has a leaf for dependency-update bot credentials or package registry access.
If ingested, avoid duplicating GitHub product background; keep the credential-governance lens.

qualifying_updates.title: Agents as both attack targets and adversaries
qualifying_updates.summary: Axios reported Bugcrowd CEO Dave Gerry's warning that enterprise AI agents should be treated as targets as well as possible adversaries. The article connects this risk to agent identity controls, enterprise tool sprawl, opaque agent action traces, and unauthorized pre-deployment agent behavior.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local wiki can use this as a governance and risk signal: agent permissions, identity, inventory, auditability, and tool approval boundaries need to be treated as operational controls, not just application security add-ons.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Agent harness guidance should explicitly inventory agent identities, reachable tools, approved systems, and auditable action traces before granting broad enterprise access.
follow_up_notes: Consider a downstream lens on agent identity and action attribution.
Route any broad OpenAI or Bugcrowd security event chronology upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenAI researcher coding-agent token spend
qualifying_updates.summary: Business Insider reported that OpenAI researchers' coding-agent usage rose sharply, with median daily token spend estimates above $600 by mid-August and 90th-percentile users above $7,000 per day. The article also noted organizational pushback against token leaderboards and indiscriminate high usage.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a current practice signal for operating-model coverage: agent adoption needs cost observability, meaningful productivity measures, and budget controls, not raw token consumption as a success metric.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Team-adoption guidance should distinguish agent intensity from delivered, production-qualified value and pair spend dashboards with outcome metrics.
follow_up_notes: Check adoption-and-operating-model for cost-governance or token-budget leaves.

qualifying_updates.title: Security review process for community agent components
qualifying_updates.summary: Express Computer reported that Tenable and OpenAI launched CyberAgents Exchange AI Inspector, a review process for community-built AI agents, skills, MCP servers, and multi-agent playbooks. The process combines model assessment, Tenable exposure tooling, and security-researcher review before enterprise deployment.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This gives the local wiki a concrete current example for governed intake of third-party agent components: pre-deployment inspection, expert review, and component registries should be part of MCP and skills adoption workflows.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Tool and skill adoption pages can treat community agent components like dependencies: inspect before use, require provenance, and reserve human security review for deployment decisions.
follow_up_notes: Look for an existing local leaf on package-install risk, MCP governance, or skill intake.
Route broad CyberAgents Exchange product details upstream.

qualifying_updates.title: Pipeline-versus-agent production litmus
qualifying_updates.summary: A DEV Community practice post argued that many production systems branded as agents are fixed pipelines with LLM calls. It proposed a control-flow litmus: if the flowchart can be drawn before execution, the system is a pipeline; reserve autonomous agency for tasks whose next step is genuinely discovered at runtime.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is directly relevant to application patterns and agent workflows because it reframes autonomy as a cost that must be justified through reproducibility, debuggability, testing, latency, and token-budget tradeoffs.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Pattern guidance can include a decision rule: implement fixed workflows for listable steps and add bounded model-chosen control only where discovery makes static flow impossible.
follow_up_notes: Potentially map to a durable leaf on workflow-first agent design or autonomy budgeting.
Community-source status means later ingest should corroborate with higher-authority engineering sources if possible.

qualifying_updates.title: Shared Knowledge MCP human review boundary
qualifying_updates.summary: A DEV Community submission described an MCP server that converts an explicitly shared AI-assistant solution into a Markdown article and GitHub pull request, leaving publication to human review. Follow-up discussion emphasized the boundary between structuring a contribution and deciding whether it is true, non-sensitive, and worth publishing.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a current, concrete source-ingest pattern for AI-assisted development knowledge: extract only with explicit sharing, keep conversations private, validate structured output, and require human review before public documentation.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Source-workflow guidance can separate assistant-mediated formatting from epistemic authority, requiring explicit user intent and human acceptance before any private solution becomes public knowledge.
follow_up_notes: Likely relevant to durable source-ingest and citation-workflow leaves.
Preserve the privacy and human-review boundary if ingested.

qualifying_updates.title: Zero-telemetry prompt cost instrumentation
qualifying_updates.summary: A DEV Community post described EcoPrompt, a client-side browser extension that estimates prompt carbon, water, energy, and API cost in real time while avoiding prompt-text capture or server routing. The author emphasized local-only measurement, soft daily budgets, and prompt batching.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This gives adoption and governance pages a lightweight pattern for agent and prompt-cost awareness: surface cost signals without collecting sensitive prompt content, and make batching or context pruning visible to developers.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Developer-facing AI cost instrumentation should minimize telemetry, avoid collecting prompt text, and make context-pruning tradeoffs understandable at the point of use.
follow_up_notes: Could support a future local practice lens on token-spend observability and privacy-preserving usage telemetry.
Verify environmental-estimation assumptions before turning this into wiki guidance.

qualifying_updates.title: Self-correcting RAG production loop
qualifying_updates.summary: DataAspirant published a practical guide mapping Corrective RAG, Self-RAG, and Adaptive-RAG into a production graph: route by difficulty, grade retrieval evidence, rewrite or search when retrieval fails, generate only from graded evidence, then check groundedness and usefulness with retry budgets.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a strong local-practice update for codebase RAG and retrieval tooling: it turns research patterns into concrete graph nodes, structured-output graders, retry caps, parallel document grading, and streaming progress cues.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Retrieval guidance can frame self-correction as a bounded workflow with typed grader outputs, explicit retry budgets, parallel grading, and instrumented failure rates.
follow_up_notes: Check retrieval-and-tools for existing RAG evaluation and grounding leaves.
Keep broad technique descriptions upstream-owned; local value is implementation practice.
